subject: Novaterra MAP & Eval Plan — payment and invoicing checkpoints
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Cole <jordan.cole@novaterra.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: Novaterra MAP & Eval Plan — payment and invoicing checkpoints

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning — great alignment on scope and success criteria for the 8-week evaluation. I attached a proposed mutual action plan (MAP_v1) that lays out the milestones we discussed and a preliminary commercial timeline. A few points I want to make explicit so procurement can map to internal processes: 

- Pilot / Evaluation: 8 weeks, acceptance when the agreed eval prompts reach 95% pass on the baseline eval set (see MAP tab).
- Ramp / Commit: If Novaterra signs a committed capacity at the end of the pilot, we propose a three-month paid ramp (50% -> 75% -> 100%).
- Pricing & Discounts: We can offer a 12% ramp discount if you commit to a 12-month consumption minimum at the end of the pilot. Early PO/commit inside 14 days of signature unlocks an additional 3% credit.
- Payment terms: Redwood standard is Net30. For larger enterprise procurement we can be flexible — proposed concession ladder in the MAP (Net30 baseline, Net45 for 12mo commit, Net60 only with a signed PO + extended commit).
- Invoicing cadence: Monthly in arrears by default; we can do quarterly invoicing if requested but that will require a small administrative surcharge.
- PO requirements & billing start: We prefer a PO before the first invoice. If procurement needs to delay PO issuance, billing start can be anchored to the Accepted Evaluation milestone or the date we begin paid ramp (whichever is later).

Can you confirm Novaterra's procurement timing and whether Net60 is a hard requirement? If Net60 is required, procurement should confirm the PO timing and whether there is room for a minimum commit to offset the cash timing.

Attached: Novaterra_MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Next steps I suggest: 1) Procurement confirms preferred payment term and PO timing, 2) We lock MAP and SOW, 3) Legal/Docs to send final SOW + DocuSign.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior GTM Ops
Redwood Inference

--

From: Jordan Cole <jordan.cole@novaterra.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novaterra.ai
Date: 2026-03-16T04:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Novaterra MAP & Eval Plan — payment and invoicing checkpoints

Mina — thanks for sending this over and for the clear MAP. I reviewed with procurement. A few things from our side: 

- Procurement policy requires Net60 for new vendors as a default. We can sometimes accelerate to Net45 if there's an early PO and a billing hold until the PO is issued.
- We prefer quarterly invoicing aligned to our internal SAP cycles. Monthly invoices are possible but add reconciliation overhead.
- PO: Procurement will raise a PO, but timelines are ~7-10 business days after contract signature. Will that window be acceptable? We cannot guarantee PO before the pilot starts.
- Billing start: We need billing to start at the beginning of the production ramp, not necessarily the acceptance milestone — our internal launch is scheduled one week after acceptance to complete security gating.

If Net60 is a blocker, we should understand the tradeoffs (e.g., required minimum commitment, advanced payment, or escrow).

I'll loop in the procurement contact above for availability.

—Jordan
Jordan Cole
Head of AI Ops, Novaterra

Date: 2026-03-16T09:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Novaterra MAP & Eval Plan — internal note on payment requests

Mina / Marcus — quick internal take after Jordan's note from procurement. Key tradeoffs and a suggested concession path: 

- Net60 ask is common; we should avoid a flat Net60 without compensation. Offer Net45 as the standard enterprise concession.
- If Novaterra insists on Net60, require either: (a) a 12-month minimum commit or (b) a 6-month prepayment (credit applied monthly).
- PO timing: we should accept a PO within 10 business days post-signature; if PO is delayed beyond that, billing start will default to the accepted evaluation milestone and invoices will be issued per our standard cadence. This reduces revenue recognition ambiguity.
- Ramp discounts: keep the 12% commitment discount but make the additional 3% early-PO credit contingent on receipt of PO within 14 calendar days of signature.

I'll attach a short pricing note with scenarios so finance/legal can weigh in.

Karthik
Account Executive — East
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: pricing_notes_0316.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Cole <jordan.cole@novaterra.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-16T12:05:00Z
Subject: Redwood Finance — proposed payment & invoicing terms for Novaterra

Jordan — hi, Marcus Lin from Redwood Finance. Following Mina and Karthik's note, here is our formal position so procurement can map internally: 

1) Payment terms: We can accept Net45 as a standard enterprise concession. Net60 will be considered only if Novaterra provides one of the following: a) a 12-month committed minimum (signed) OR b) a 6-month prepayment schedule.

2) PO requirement: We require a customer PO before the first invoice to apply the early-PO credit. If a PO cannot be produced before the first invoice, we will hold first invoice generation until we reach the Accepted Evaluation milestone; however, services consumed during the pilot will be documented and invoiced retroactively once the PO is in place.

3) Invoicing cadence: Monthly in arrears is our default. We can provide quarterly invoices but there will be a one-time administrative fee equivalent to 1.5% of the first quarter's invoice value to cover reconciliation overhead.

4) Billing start: Billing shall begin on the earlier of (i) the Accepted Evaluation milestone date OR (ii) the date the paid ramp begins, provided a PO has been received. If a PO arrives after either of these dates, Redwood will invoice retroactively to the applicable billing start date.

5) Discounts: The 12% ramp discount is applied if Novaterra commits to a 12-month minimum within 7 days of the end-of-pilot signature. The 3% early-PO credit is applied only if we receive the PO within 14 calendar days of the signature date.

Please confirm if Novaterra accepts Net45 with the above PO/billing start language. If procurement requires Net60 without commit, we will need to route to CRO/Finance for an exception and may require an extended commitment to offset DSO risk.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Finance — Redwood Inference
finance@redwood.ai

--
Attachment: terms_summary_0316.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Jordan Cole <jordan.cole@novaterra.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@novaterra.ai
Date: 2026-03-16T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood Finance — proposed payment & invoicing terms for Novaterra

Marcus / Mina — thanks for the clarity. Procurement confirms Net60 is preferred, but they can accept Net45 if we provide a 12-month minimum commit. Two quick clarifications: 

- PO timing: procurement will raise a PO within 7-10 business days post-signature. That's aligned with what I shared.
- Billing start: we want billing to align to the production ramp date (one week after acceptance). If Redwood needs billing to be tied to the acceptance milestone to protect revenue recognition, procurement asks that the invoices be scheduled to the production ramp date in the SOW. We can make the PO reflect that alignment when we issue it.

Assuming Redwood can accept Net45 with a 12-month commit trigger, we are happy to proceed to signature. Please send the SOW and DocuSign link and we'll get procurement moving.

—Jordan
